results_kept.title: systemd-cryptenroll - ArchWiki
results_kept.snippet: systemd-cryptenroll allows enrolling smartcards, FIDO2 tokens and Trusted Platform Module security chips into LUKS devices, as well as regular passphrases. These devices are later unlocked by systemd-cryptsetup@.service, using the enrolled tokens.

results_kept.title: systemd-cryptenroll: Unlock LUKS2 with TPM2, FIDO2, Recovery Key
results_kept.snippet: sudo systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-device=auto /dev/sdc1. Enroll FIDO2 HMAC token.LUKS2 volume (not LUKS1) — confirm with cryptsetup luksDump. Root or sudo. An existing unlock secret (passphrase or key file) for every enrollment except --wipe-slot.

results_kept.title: Stop Typing LUKS Passphrases at Every Boot: Practical systemd ...
results_kept.snippet: 4 days ago · systemd-cryptenroll is the operator tool for binding LUKS2 volumes to hardware factors systemd already understands at boot: TPM2 chips, FIDO2 tokens (hmac-secret), PKCS#11 smartcards, plus computer-generated recovery keys. results_kept.title: Practical Encrypted Home Directories with systemd-homed on Linux
results_kept.snippet: The result: portable .home image files you can copy to another machine, per-user encryption that locks on logout or suspend, and a cleaner separation from the host system. Why Use systemd-homed? Encryption by default (LUKS or fscrypt) for each user. Portability: A single .home file (or directory) contains the home + identity.
